voice.tone: Crisp, encouraging, product-led, and energetic; makes publishing feel simple and momentum-driven, with light emoji accents.
voice.rhythm: Short, plainspoken sentences and compact paragraphs. Often opens with a punchy claim, uses one-line paragraphs for emphasis, then lands on a memorable takeaway.
voice.person: Usually speaks as the product or as “we,” addressing the reader directly as “you.” No consistent human signature is shown.
exemplars: Most people overthink their first post. They wait for the perfect idea, the perfect words, the perfect moment. But the secret is: just start. Your first 10 posts won't be your best, and that's the whole point.

Here's what actually works: 🌱 Write about what you're learning right now 📈 Share one small insight every day 🔄 Repurpose across platforms ✨ Let your voice develop naturally Consistency beats perfection. Every single time.
The people with the biggest audiences didn't start with an audience. They started with a habit: write, publish, iterate. Your future self will thank you for starting today.

segments.name: Creator publishing across multiple social platforms
segments.situation: A creator writes social content and needs to publish or repurpose it across several supported networks.

situation_provenance.quote: Effortlessly cross-post to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Threads, and Mastodon.

segments.job_to_be_done: Write, preview, schedule, cross-post, and analyze social content from one workspace.
segments.trigger: Publishing regularly on more than one social network or wanting a more focused writing workflow.

pains.statement: Repeating the publishing workflow separately across multiple social platforms may consume time and create inconsistency.
Uncertainty about how a post, thread, mention, or media attachment will look after publishing can delay publication.

segments.name: Social media team coordinating drafts and launches
segments.situation: A team reviews drafts, coordinates a shared publishing calendar, and may need posts from multiple team members to launch together.

situation_provenance.quote: Comments, @mentions, and shared drafts make collaboration a breeze.
Schedule team posts to go live together, with Slack pings when they do.

segments.job_to_be_done: Collaboratively draft, review, schedule, and launch social posts while keeping the team aligned.
segments.trigger: A growing publishing operation requires shared review states, coordinated launches, or visibility across a team calendar.

pains.statement: Feedback and approvals can become fragmented when drafts, comments, and publishing schedules are not shared.
Coordinating several team posts to publish together may require manual timing and team notifications.
